steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Strong melodies have clear phrase structure — typically 4-bar or 8-bar phrases with a sense of question (antecedent) and answer (consequent).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Develop melodies through: sequence (repeating at a different pitch), inversion (turning upside down), augmentation (stretching), fragmentation (using part of the idea).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Match rhythm to genre: rock riffs use syncopation and repetition; Classical melodies use balanced phrasing; jazz melodies use swing and blue notes.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Staff notation requirements: you must submit a score in staff notation (up to 4 sharps/flats) — notation quality affects the AO2 mark for technical control.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how melody writing are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use melody writing. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use melody writing in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their | A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how melody writing are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comparative language. | A practical application showing understanding of how melody writing can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended effect.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
